title: Attitude, manner and standards
summary: Describing how people act and what they act according to: 'as if to say' ({とばかりに}, {んばかり}), complaining about someone ({ときたら}), defying obstacles ({をものともせず}), 'in one's own way' ({なりに}), 'in line with' ({に即[そく]して}), saying things boldly ({てはばからない}) and doing things absent-mindedly ({ともなく}).

points.title: 〜とばかりに
points.meaning: as if to say; as though (X)
points.structure: Quotation / plain form (often a command or volitional) + とばかりに
points.explanation:
{〜とばかりに} describes an action that silently communicates a message: someone doesn't actually say X, but their behaviour all but says it. 'He turned his back on me as if to say "Go home".'

The X is often a short quote, command or exclamation: {早[はや]く帰[かえ]れ}, {待[ま]ってました}, {いい加減[かげん]にしろ}. The fixed phrase {ここぞとばかりに} means 'seizing the moment, as if to say "this is it!"'.

It describes other people's actions, not your own.

**Register:** written and narrative, but also common in vivid storytelling and TV narration.

examples.jp: 待[ま]ってましたとばかりに、子[こ]どもたちはプールに飛[と]び込[こ]んだ。
examples.en: As if they'd been waiting for that moment, the children leapt into the pool.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は「もう帰[かえ]れ」とばかりに、私[わたし]に背[せ]を向[む]けた。
examples.en: He turned his back on me as if to say, 'Go home.'

examples.jp: 店員[てんいん]は早[はや]く出[で]て行[い]けとばかりに、閉店[へいてん]の準備[じゅんび]を始[はじ]めた。
examples.en: The shop staff started getting ready to close, as if to say 'Hurry up and leave.'

examples.jp: ここぞとばかりに、彼[かれ]は日頃[ひごろ]の不満[ふまん]をぶちまけた。
examples.en: Seizing his chance, he poured out all his usual complaints.

points.notes: Compare {〜んばかり} (next point): {とばかりに} follows a quote; {んばかり} follows a verb stem and means 'almost doing'. {言[い]わんばかりに} and {とばかりに} are often interchangeable.

quiz.q: 母[はは]は「いい加減[かげん]にしなさい」＿＿、テレビを消[け]した。
quiz.en: My mother switched off the TV as if to say, 'That's enough!'

quiz.q: セールが始[はじ]まると、客[きゃく]たちはここぞ＿＿売[う]り場[ば]に殺到[さっとう]した。
quiz.en: When the sale began, the customers seized their moment and rushed to the counters.

points.title: 〜んばかり
points.meaning: almost; as if about to; on the verge of
points.structure: Verb ない-stem + んばかり(に／の／だ) (する → せんばかり)
points.explanation:
{〜んばかり} combines classical volitional {ん} with {ばかり}: 'just about to do X'. It describes something so intense it seems to be on the verge of X, though X doesn't actually happen: {泣[な]き出[だ]さんばかり} 'on the verge of tears', {割[わ]れんばかりの拍手[はくしゅ]} 'thunderous applause (as if the hall would split)'.

{言[い]わんばかりに} 'as if to say' is extremely common: {帰[かえ]れと言[い]わんばかりに}.

**Register:** literary and descriptive — novels, news, sports commentary. {割[わ]れんばかりの拍手[はくしゅ]} and {言[い]わんばかり} are set phrases worth learning.

examples.jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は泣[な]き出[だ]さんばかりの顔[かお]で、私[わたし]を見[み]つめた。
examples.en: She stared at me, looking as if she was about to burst into tears.

examples.jp: 優勝[ゆうしょう]が決[き]まった瞬間[しゅんかん]、会場[かいじょう]は割[わ]れんばかりの拍手[はくしゅ]に包[つつ]まれた。
examples.en: The moment the victory was decided, the venue erupted in thunderous applause.

examples.jp: 店主[てんしゅ]は、二度[にど]と来[く]るなと言[い]わんばかりに、私[わたし]たちをにらんだ。
examples.en: The shop owner glared at us as if to say 'Never come back.'

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は今[いま]にも殴[なぐ]りかからんばかりの勢[いきお]いで怒鳴[どな]った。
examples.en: He yelled as though he were about to throw a punch at any moment.

points.notes: Forms: {〜んばかりに} + verb, {〜んばかりの} + noun, {〜んばかりだ} at the end of a sentence.

quiz.q: コンサートの最後[さいご]に、会場[かいじょう]は割[わ]れ＿＿拍手[はくしゅ]に包[つつ]まれた。
quiz.en: At the end of the concert, the hall was filled with thunderous applause.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]は「お前[まえ]が悪[わる]い」と言[い]わ＿＿、私[わたし]をにらみつけた。
quiz.en: He glared at me as if to say 'It's your fault.'

points.title: 〜ときたら
points.meaning: speaking of X (exasperated); when it comes to X (complaint)
points.explanation:
{〜ときたら} raises a topic in order to complain about it. The topic is usually someone close (husband, kids, boss) or something annoying (the weather, an old computer), and what follows is a criticism or expression of frustration.

It's very subjective and emotional: 'My husband, honestly — he just sleeps all day on his days off.'

**Register:** conversational! Unlike most N1 grammar, you'll genuinely hear this in everyday chat, especially among friends and in TV dramas. It's not used in formal writing. It also has a less common positive use with food and drink ({夏[なつ]のビールときたら最高[さいこう]だ}).

examples.jp: この古[ふる]いパソコンときたら、すぐ固[かた]まるんだから。
examples.en: This old computer, honestly — it freezes all the time.

examples.jp: うちの夫[おっと]ときたら、休[やす]みの日[ひ]は一日中[いちにちじゅう]寝[ね]てばかりいる。
examples.en: My husband, I tell you — on his days off he just sleeps all day.

examples.jp: あの店[みせ]の店員[てんいん]ときたら、客[きゃく]が来[き]ても挨拶[あいさつ]一[ひと]つしない。
examples.en: The staff at that shop don't even say hello when customers come in.

examples.jp: 最近[さいきん]の天気[てんき]ときたら、暑[あつ]かったり寒[さむ]かったりで本当[ほんとう]に困[こま]る。
examples.en: The weather lately — hot one day, cold the next. It's really annoying.

points.notes: Not for yourself, and not for neutral topics. For a neutral 'speaking of', use {〜といえば}.

quiz.q: うちの息子[むすこ]＿＿、ゲームばかりして全然[ぜんぜん]勉強[べんきょう]しない。
quiz.en: My son, honestly — he does nothing but play games and never studies.

quiz.q: あの政治家[せいじか]＿＿、言[い]うことがころころ変[か]わる。
quiz.en: That politician, honestly — what he says changes all the time.

points.title: 〜をものともせず(に)
points.meaning: undaunted by; in defiance of; making light of
points.structure: Noun (obstacle) + をものともせず(に)
points.explanation:
{〜をものともせず} means 'not treating X as anything to worry about' — bravely pushing through difficulties: injury, storms, opposition, danger. It expresses admiration for the person's courage or determination.

It describes others (or a group) from an observer's point of view, so it's not used to describe yourself.

**Register:** written and formal; very common in news and sports reporting ({けがをものともせず} 'shrugging off an injury').

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は足[あし]のけがをものともせず、最後[さいご]まで走[はし]り抜[ぬ]いた。
examples.en: Undaunted by his leg injury, he ran all the way to the finish.

examples.jp: 周囲[しゅうい]の反対[はんたい]をものともせずに、彼女[かのじょ]は起業[きぎょう]した。
examples.en: Brushing aside the opposition of those around her, she started her own business.

examples.jp: 救助隊[きゅうじょたい]は激[はげ]しい雨[あめ]をものともせず、行方[ゆくえ]不明者[ふめいしゃ]の捜索[そうさく]を続[つづ]けた。
examples.en: Undeterred by the heavy rain, the rescue team continued searching for the missing.

examples.jp: 数々[かずかず]の困難[こんなん]をものともせず、二人[ふたり]は夢[ゆめ]を実現[じつげん]させた。
examples.en: Overcoming countless difficulties, the two of them made their dream come true.

points.notes: {をものともせず} = admirable courage against obstacles; {をよそに} (Unit 10) = ignoring other people's worries, often critical.

quiz.q: その登山家[とざんか]は、零下[れいか]三十度[さんじゅうど]の寒[さむ]さ＿＿、頂上[ちょうじょう]を目指[めざ]した。
quiz.en: Undaunted by the cold of minus thirty degrees, the climber pushed on toward the summit.

quiz.q: 選手[せんしゅ]たちは強風[きょうふう]をものとも＿＿、全力[ぜんりょく]でプレーした。
quiz.en: Undeterred by the strong wind, the players gave it their all.

points.title: 〜なりに／〜なりの
points.meaning: in one's own way; as best one can (given one's limits)
points.structure: Noun / plain form + なりに (+ Verb) / なりの (+ Noun)
points.explanation:
{〜なりに} means 'in a way that suits X, within X's limits'. It acknowledges that X isn't perfect or fully capable, but still makes an effort or has a valid perspective: {子[こ]どもは子[こ]どもなりに} 'kids, in their own way', {私[わたし]なりに考[かんが]えた} 'I thought about it as best I could'.

Repeating the noun ({子[こ]どもは子[こ]どもなりに}) is very common. {〜なりの} modifies a noun: {彼[かれ]なりの理由[りゆう]} 'his own reasons'.

**Register:** neutral and very common in everyday conversation and business. {私[わたし]なりに} is a humble, useful phrase for meetings: 'here's my take'.

examples.jp: 私[わたし]なりに考[かんが]えてみたのですが、この案[あん]はどうでしょうか。
examples.en: I've given it some thought in my own way — how about this idea?

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]には彼[かれ]なりの事情[じじょう]があるのだろう。
examples.en: He probably has his own reasons.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもは子[こ]どもなりに、親[おや]のことを心配[しんぱい]しているものだ。
examples.en: Children worry about their parents in their own way.

examples.jp: 給料[きゅうりょう]は少[すく]ないが、少[すく]ないなりに工夫[くふう]して生活[せいかつ]している。
examples.en: My salary is small, but I get by with a bit of ingenuity.

points.notes: Don't confuse with {ならでは} 'unique to' (Unit 6) — {ならでは} is high praise; {なりに} admits limitations. Also different from {なり} 'as soon as' (Unit 1).

quiz.q: 新人[しんじん]は新人[しんじん]＿＿、精一杯[せいいっぱい]頑張[がんば]っている。
quiz.en: The newcomers are doing their best in their own way.

quiz.q: 結果[けっか]は出[で]なかったが、自分[じぶん]＿＿努力[どりょく]はしたつもりだ。
quiz.en: I didn't get results, but I believe I made an effort in my own way.

points.title: 〜に即[そく]して／〜に即[そく]した
points.meaning: in line with; in accordance with (facts, reality, rules)
points.structure: Noun + に即[そく]して (+ Verb) / に即[そく]した (+ Noun)
points.explanation:
{即[そく]する} means 'to conform to, to be based on'. {X に即[そく]して} means 'closely following X' — where X is facts, reality, actual conditions, experience or rules: {事実[じじつ]に即[そく]して} 'based on the facts', {実情[じつじょう]に即[そく]した政策[せいさく]} 'policy suited to actual conditions'.

The idea is matching a plan or explanation to concrete reality, rather than theory.

**Register:** formal; very common in business, government and academic writing. Also written {則[そく]して} when the standard is a rule or law.

examples.jp: 事実[じじつ]に即[そく]して、事故[じこ]の経緯[けいい]を説明[せつめい]してください。
examples.en: Please explain how the accident happened, sticking to the facts.

examples.jp: 実情[じつじょう]に即[そく]した政策[せいさく]が求[もと]められている。
examples.en: Policies that reflect the actual situation are needed.

examples.jp: 規則[きそく]に即[そく]して処理[しょり]しなければならない。
examples.en: This must be handled in accordance with the rules.

examples.jp: 学生[がくせい]のレベルに即[そく]した教材[きょうざい]を使[つか]うべきだ。
examples.en: We should use teaching materials suited to the students' level.

points.notes: Similar: {〜に沿[そ]って} (along the lines of) and {〜に基[もと]づいて} (based on). {に即[そく]して} stresses close fit with reality.

quiz.q: 法律[ほうりつ]は、時代[じだい]の変化[へんか]＿＿見直[みなお]されるべきだ。
quiz.en: Laws should be revised in line with the changing times.

quiz.q: 机上[きじょう]の空論[くうろん]ではなく、現場[げんば]の実態[じったい]に＿＿対策[たいさく]が必要[ひつよう]だ。
quiz.en: We need measures that match the reality on the ground, not armchair theories.

points.title: 〜てはばからない
points.meaning: to not hesitate to (say); to boldly / shamelessly (declare)
points.structure: Verb て-form (言[い]う・公言[こうげん]する etc.) + はばからない
points.explanation:
{はばかる} means 'to hold back out of consideration or fear'. {〜てはばからない} means 'to say or do X openly, without any hesitation' — even though others might find it bold, arrogant or controversial.

It mostly combines with verbs of speaking: {言[い]う}, {公言[こうげん]する} (declare publicly), {断言[だんげん]する} (assert), {口[くち]にする}. Depending on context, it can sound admiring (confident) or critical (shameless).

**Register:** written and formal — news, profiles, criticism.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は「自分[じぶん]は天才[てんさい]だ」と公言[こうげん]してはばからない。
examples.en: He openly declares that he's a genius.

examples.jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は、仕事[しごと]より家族[かぞく]が大事[だいじ]だと言[い]ってはばからない。
examples.en: She doesn't hesitate to say that her family matters more than her work.

examples.jp: 社長[しゃちょう]は「失敗[しっぱい]を恐[おそ]れるな」と口[くち]にしてはばからない。
examples.en: The president never hesitates to say, 'Don't be afraid of failure.'

examples.jp: その政治家[せいじか]は、差別的[さべつてき]な発言[はつげん]を繰[く]り返[かえ]してはばからない。
examples.en: That politician shamelessly keeps making discriminatory remarks.

points.notes: Related: {人目[ひとめ]をはばからず} 'without caring who's watching' ({人目[ひとめ]をはばからず泣[な]いた} 'cried openly in front of everyone').

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]は自分[じぶん]こそが次[つぎ]の社長[しゃちょう]にふさわしいと言[い]って＿＿。
quiz.en: He openly says that he's the one best suited to be the next president.

quiz.q: その評論家[ひょうろんか]は、日本[にほん]映画[えいが]は世界一[せかいいち]だと公言[こうげん]して＿＿。
quiz.en: The critic openly declares that Japanese cinema is the best in the world.

points.title: 〜ともなく／〜ともなしに
points.meaning: without really meaning to; absent-mindedly; from somewhere (unknown)
points.structure: Verb (dictionary form) + ともなく + same verb / Question word (+ particle) + ともなく
points.explanation:
{〜ともなく} has two uses:

**1. Verb + {ともなく} + same verb:** doing something without any particular intention, absent-mindedly: {見[み]るともなく見[み]ていた} 'was half-watching', {聞[き]くともなしに聞[き]いていた} 'overheard without really listening'. Usually with perception verbs (see, hear, think).

**2. Question word + {ともなく}:** the source is unclear: {どこからともなく} 'from somewhere or other', {誰[だれ]からともなく} 'without anyone in particular starting it', {いつからともなく} 'at some point'.

**Register:** literary and descriptive — novels, essays. {どこからともなく} is common in storytelling generally.

examples.jp: どこからともなく、いい匂[にお]いが漂[ただよ]ってきた。
examples.en: A lovely smell came drifting from somewhere.

examples.jp: 見[み]るともなくテレビを見[み]ていたら、昔[むかし]の友人[ゆうじん]が映[うつ]っていた。
examples.en: I was half-watching TV when an old friend appeared on the screen.

examples.jp: 聞[き]くともなしに隣[となり]の席[せき]の会話[かいわ]を聞[き]いていた。
examples.en: Without really meaning to, I was listening to the conversation at the next table.

examples.jp: 誰[だれ]からともなく拍手[はくしゅ]が起[お]こり、やがて会場[かいじょう]全体[ぜんたい]に広[ひろ]がった。
examples.en: Applause started from no one in particular and soon spread through the whole hall.

points.notes: Don't confuse with {ともなると} 'when it comes to' (Unit 6).

quiz.q: 窓[まど]の外[そと]を眺[なが]める＿＿眺[なが]めていると、一羽[いちわ]の鳥[とり]が飛[と]んできた。
quiz.en: As I was absent-mindedly gazing out of the window, a bird flew over.

quiz.q: どこから＿＿、子[こ]どもたちの歌声[うたごえ]が聞[き]こえてきた。
quiz.en: From somewhere, the sound of children singing reached us.
